mcq.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes FDI from FPI?
options: FDI involves a lasting interest and a say in management, while FPI is a financial investment without control
FPI always involves building new factories
FDI is always short-term and speculative
There is no difference between them
mcq.explain: Foreign direct investment brings a lasting interest and significant influence or control over the management of an enterprise, and is usually long-term. Foreign portfolio investment is investment in securities for financial returns, without control, and is more liquid and volatile.
mcq.topic: Foreign portfolio investment (FPI) and the FDI–FPI contrast
mcq.fast: FDI = control + long-term; FPI = financial + liquid.

mcq.q: In India, an investment by a foreign investor in a listed Indian company is generally classified as FDI when it is:
options: 10% or more of the company's post-issue paid-up equity capital
mcq.explain: Under Indian foreign investment rules, investment of less than 10% of the post-issue paid-up equity capital of a listed company by a foreign portfolio investor is portfolio investment. When the holding reaches 10% or more, it is treated as foreign direct investment. The threshold reflects the idea of a lasting interest.
mcq.topic: Foreign portfolio investment (FPI) and the FDI–FPI contrast
mcq.fast: 10% threshold: below = FPI, 10% or more = FDI.

mcq.q: A foreign company builds a brand-new factory in India from scratch. This mode of FDI is called:
mcq.explain: Greenfield investment means setting up entirely new facilities in the host country. Brownfield investment means acquiring or merging with an existing enterprise, or leasing existing facilities. Portfolio investment and external commercial borrowings are not modes of FDI.
mcq.fast: New from scratch = greenfield; buy existing = brownfield.

mcq.q: An Indian car maker sets up a plant abroad to make the same cars it makes at home. This is:
mcq.explain: Horizontal FDI occurs when a firm replicates the same activity abroad that it carries out at home, often to serve the foreign market directly. Vertical FDI occurs when a firm locates a different stage of its production chain abroad, such as sourcing raw materials or components.
mcq.fast: Same activity abroad = horizontal; different stage = vertical.

mcq.q: Which of these is commonly cited as a problem of FDI for the host country?
options: Large outflow of profits and royalties to the parent company abroad
mcq.explain: FDI brings capital, technology and jobs, but critics point to the repatriation of large profits, royalties and fees to parent companies, possible crowding out of domestic firms, and loss of control over key sectors. Transfer of technology, job creation and capital formation are benefits, not problems.
mcq.topic: Problems with FDI, safeguards, and FDI in India
mcq.fast: FDI problem = profit repatriation, domestic firms crowded out.

mcq.q: Under India's FDI policy, investment under the "automatic route" means:
options: Prior approval of the government is always needed
No prior approval of the government or RBI is needed
Investment is allowed only in government bonds
mcq.explain: Under the automatic route, a foreign investor can invest without prior approval of the government or the RBI, subject to sectoral caps and conditions, and only needs to report the investment. Under the government (approval) route, prior approval of the government is required.
mcq.topic: Problems with FDI, safeguards, and FDI in India
